answer: Make first settlement a bonded berth. A newcomer deposits collateral and may clear invoices only through a public harbor until a thirty-day horizon lapses. Each week a clerk draws yarrow stalks to pick three unaffiliated inspectors who share no sponsor; they confirm the newcomer was paid by distinct principals for work those principals actually received. If one wallet cluster underwrites many names, or invoices recur across aliases, the deposit is burned and the berth is revoked. Every alias then needs its own collateral, paying principals, and an inspection record a sibling cannot reuse.
